evidence.description: ISO8601DateFormatter is instantiated every time lastUpdatedDate() is called, which is an expensive operation.

candidates.explanation: Creating a new DateFormatter instance inside a function that is called repeatedly (e.g., during a loop of results) is a performance anti-pattern. It should be reused or stored as a static property.
candidates.title: Inefficient DateFormatter instantiation

evidence.description: The code manually iterates through a results array and uses a switch statement to map values to specific properties, despite the data structure already being decodable.

candidates.explanation: The manual mapping logic creates a maintenance burden. If the API structure changes, multiple points in the switch statement may need updates. Using a more direct decoding strategy or a dictionary-based approach would be more scalable.
candidates.title: Redundant data decoding and manual mapping

evidence.description: Dates are initialized using hardcoded Unix timestamps.
Dates are initialized using hardcoded Unix timestamps.

candidates.explanation: Hardcoding timestamps makes the code difficult to maintain and reason about. These values should ideally be fetched from a configuration file or a remote source.
candidates.title: Hardcoded date strings in property initialization
